page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 12 dedicated physical cores without multithreading powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor operating at 5.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features AVX-512 extensions and advanced cache manipulation flags. The instance delivers a massive 384.0 GB pool of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding a resource ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight leading single-threaded throughput, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core measurements ranking in the top ten percent. Multi-core performance across the 12 dedicated cores delivers strong results in Geekbench multi-core tests and compression workloads. Uncached DDR5 memory bandwidth achieves strong marks at 204.42 GB/sec for reads and 136.09 GB/sec for writes across 256 MB blocks, supporting high-throughput data processing and fast text generation during inference tests.

From an efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-CPU ratio eliminates the need to pay for surplus compute cores simply to accommodate large working datasets. The presence of local NVMe storage further enhances throughput for disk-spilling operations without requiring remote block attachment. The hardware footprint is optimized for large in-memory databases, caching layers, real-time analytics, and data pipeline transformations.
description: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.3xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based instance designed for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R05 processor running at 5.0 GHz, the instance delivers 12 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It provides an exceptional memory capacity of 384.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, establishing a 32.0 GB per core ratio. An integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD provides rapid ephemeral storage alongside a 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system achieves top-tier single-core benchmark scores in Geekbench and stress-ng, accompanied by strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 204 GB/sec for reads and 136 GB/sec for writes. The high RAM-to-core ratio allows organizations to scale memory-resident applications efficiently without overprovisioning compute resources. This architecture is well suited for large in-memory key-value stores, distributed database caches, memory-constrained data science tasks, and intensive ETL data processing.
